BLOCKER: AC-4 quota enforcement is entirely absent: no `internal/limits/quota.go`, no call sites, and nothing emits `edp_quota_allowed_total`/`edp_quota_denials_total` yet the alert `ProductForgeQuotaDenied` and dashboard panel 5 query them — AC-4 cannot be satisfied and the alert can never fire.

AC-1 baseline evidence declared in the contract (`engineering/benchmarks/BI-PF-1314/README.md`, `db/local/baseline.json`, `db/local/metrics.prom`) is not in the diff, and `config/edp-slo.json` contains thresholds with no baseline ID reference — violates the "SLO thresholds are set from measured baselines, not invented targets" invariant.

Store metrics and degradation are dead code: `observe.Recorder` and `degrade.Check` have no store-adapter call sites in the diff, so AC-3/AC-4 ("demonstrated per store") and the runtime contract `store adapter -> degrade.Check -> fixed degraded error + observe metrics` are unproven.
MAJOR: `bench.Compare` ignores `MaxError` when a result has an error (`if r.Err != "" { violation; continue }`), and `MaxError==0` is treated as "unset" in the group override — `max_errors` config is effectively dead.
`edp_store_latency_ms` is emitted as a last-value gauge via `Set`, not the histogram the observability contract requires; p95/p99 store SLOs are therefore impossible from this metric.
`edp_bench_errors_total` is written as 0/1 per run from a file sink — non-monotonic value under a `_total` counter name, so any `rate()`/`increase()` over it is wrong.
`observe.Recorder.Request` passes the caller-supplied `outcome` string straight into a label with no allowlist; only `store` is bounded, so cardinality/leak risk remains.
`ProductForgeBenchmarkLatencyRegression` hardcodes `> 500` while `config/edp-slo.json` sets db to 250 — rules are hand-written, not generated/validated for drift against config as Slice 4 requires.
`db_explain_capture.py` validates but never enforces `--per-minute` or any concurrency cap; the design invariant requires both probability and per-minute/concurrency budgets.

No audit record (actor, statement label, sample decision, artifact path) is produced for EXPLAIN runs, and `--out` writes to an arbitrary path with no retention/access-control enforcement — violates the audit/security contract.

Production cap is client-asserted: `--env` defaults to `PF_ENV`/`dev`, so a mis-set env allows `--sample-rate 0.1` against production; no separate explicit prod-enable switch as the non-goal requires.
`expires_at` renewal tracking/"renewals are alerted and bounded" is not implemented; `Config` is loaded once with no reload path, so operators cannot force-expire without a redeploy.

`config/edp-slo.schema.json` and `config/edp-degradation.schema.json` (contract + CTL-CONFIG-SCHEMA) are missing; `validate_edp_slo.py` only asserts alert names/panel presence, which is a tautological no-drift check.

`[OUT_OF_SCOPE]` `scripts/dev/review_ledger.py` now returns `[]` when no delta entries exist, silently disabling the `FULL_REVIEW_MISSING` gate for delta items (review-tooling behavior change, CL-002 territory).
MINOR: `config/edp-degradation.json` has `"stores": {}` — no per-store switch demonstrated and the test loop is vacuous.

Bench scenario semantics silently changed (`kind 'note'→'semantic'`, `acl_scope 'team'→'project'`) with no rationale; this alters what is measured and is close to the out-of-scope "data-model changes of the stores" line.
Freshness alert `time() - edp_bench_last_run_unixtime > 86400` never fires when the metric is absent; needs an `absent()` companion for a never-run suite.
`cmd/bench` default `-baseline config/edp-slo.json` is cwd-relative while the documented invocation runs from `go/edpsvc`; only the doc example's explicit path saves it.
No `Load` validation test for `expires_at` exceeding `max_duration_seconds` or for `max_errors` handling; `slo_test` only exercises `Compare` happy paths.
EXPLAIN redaction is regex-only (quoted literals, 4+ digit numbers); UUIDs/emails/timestamps outside quotes and `tenant_id` column values in plan output are not covered.
`max_errors` sentinel ambiguity and lack of `p50` budget in config mean partial budget semantics are undocumented.
NIT: `psycopg` is imported lazily with no pinned dependency/requirements entry for the tooling path.
`PrometheusSink` overwrites the sink file per run; there is no rotation or run-id comment header for traceability.
`validate_edp_slo.py` hardcodes `REQUIRED_GROUPS` including `artifact` while bench `scenarios()` groups are not cross-checked against config.
SUMMARY: Direction is right: bounded labels, fail-closed degradation errors, sampled EXPLAIN guard, and offline asset validation are solid foundations.

Not mergeable as-is: quota enforcement is missing entirely (AC-4), baseline evidence artifacts and baseline-ID linkage are absent (AC-1), and neither metrics nor degradation is wired into store adapters, so AC-3/AC-4 are only unit-tested, not demonstrated.

Observability contract mismatches (gauge latency, non-monotonic `_total`, hand-written rule thresholds) will let SLO drift go undetected; fix before the EDP-24 evidence gate relies on these baselines.
